body:
A split that happens inside a driven flow strands its own children: the parent goes terminal (`close-disposition = split`), the children materialise on disk fully briefed — and the run that caused all of this never drives them. The operator restarts with `pdca flow <child-ids>` by hand. The planner's own runtime prompt documents the limitation instead of the harness fixing it:

> "A CSV-DRIVEN batch run re-enumerates every in-flight bundle from disk after the Plan beat, so it picks the children up […] EVERY OTHER SHAPE, including an explicit id list like `pdca flow 500 501`, drives exactly the ids it was given and never looks for new ones; `--accept` prints the `pdca flow <child-ids>` command that drives them." (`leaves.py`, `_plan_prompt`)

## Where the drive set freezes

- `flow.flow_ids` builds `bundles` from exactly the listed ids, once, then hands the fixed list to `_drive_and_act`. A split during the run adds children the list never contains.
- `flow.flow` (single id) loops on the one bundle; when the Plan session splits it, the parent derives terminal and the loop exits. The children sit PLANNED, undriven.
- `_drive_and_act` computes `wave_list = waves.compute_waves(cfg, bundles)` once, up front. Even the CSV batch — the one shape that does pick up children — only re-enumerates *between Plan and drive* (`flow_batch` globs after `do_plan_batch`). A split that arrives during the drive phase (the documented Entry-B path: `iterate-plan` at sign-off → re-plan → split) is adopted by **no** mode; it waits for the next invocation.

So the two backstop entries of the size-and-split design (docs 07, "Size & split") both end in a restart: the mechanism that decomposes work mid-flight has no way to hand the pieces back to the flight it is part of.

## Ask

When a bundle in the drive set reaches `close-disposition = split`, the flow should adopt its children instead of stranding them:

1. **Detect** — after a wave drives (or after a Plan/re-plan beat), check the just-terminal bundles for the split disposition and enumerate their children. Today the child ids live in prose in the parent's `build-notes.md`; a machine-readable children record written at `--accept` (see the companion sizer filing's lineage breadcrumb — same artifact, both directions) makes this a read, not a parse.
2. **Validate** — run the children through the same `waves.partition_schedulable` tolerance the batch resume path already uses: a child with an unresolvable dependency is held loudly, never aborts the run.
3. **Splice** — recompute the remaining waves with the children included, honouring their `Depends on` / `Conflicts with`. This is the part that needs care with `_drive_and_act`'s run-scoped integration state: children join *after* the current wave, point at the same per-target integration branch via the existing `_point_at_integration` reconciliation, and count against the same run's `max_passes` budget rather than resetting it.
4. **Report** — the adoption is loud: "issue_X split → adopted children issue_Y, issue_Z into wave k+1", so a batch remains explainable as one unit.

Applies to all three entry points (`flow`, `flow_ids`, `flow_batch`'s drive phase). The `--accept` hint printing `pdca flow <child-ids>` stays — it is still the right remedy for a split accepted *outside* any running flow.

Behavioural guard-rails that should hold by construction:

- Adoption is bounded: children adopted this run can themselves split, so the adoption loop shares the run's existing iteration budget — no unbounded recursion (the companion sizer filing addresses *why* recursive splits happen at all; this issue must merely not enable an infinite one).
- An explicit-id flow adopts only children *of the ids it was given* (transitively). It never widens into a disk sweep — that distinction between `flow_ids` and the CSV sweep is deliberate and stays.

## Companion filing

Filed together with #448 (split children re-score oversized on fields the split itself installs). Its lineage/children breadcrumb is the natural detection artifact for step 1 here.
title: flow cannot adopt split children mid-run — a split inside an explicit-id flow requires restarting the flow with the child ids
